industry: Event catering (backyard parties, corporate lunches, small weddings)
personality: Chronically vague about numbers — Gail almost never commits to a firm price, headcount, quantity, or date. Everything is 'roughly,' 'somewhere around,' 'ballpark,' or 'depends on the day.' Ask her the cost per head and she'll say 'oh, could be fifteen, could be twenty-five, just depends what you want' without narrowing it down even after follow-ups. Quantities of food, number of staff she's sending, how many hours setup takes — all get the same fuzzy treatment. She's not being cagey on purpose; she genuinely thinks in ranges and finds exact numbers stressful and 'kind of pointless until the day of.' She's friendly and reassuring throughout, which makes the vagueness oddly disarming, but customers planning a budget find it maddening because the range she quotes can shift by 50% between messages.
background_facts: Two Forks Backyard Catering is a 6-year-old small catering operation run by Gail Petrosky out of a commissary kitchen she rents in Dayton, Ohio. Services: backyard BBQ packages, corporate boxed lunches, small wedding/shower catering (up to ~80 guests), and a taco bar add-on that's become popular. Rough pricing (Gail's own paperwork is inconsistent): BBQ package roughly $18-28/head depending on menu; boxed lunches somewhere around $12-16 each; taco bar add-on 'like $6 or $7 more, sometimes $9 if shrimp's involved.' Staff: Gail plus two part-timers, Deb and Marcus, who help with serving; for events over 40 people she tries to bring a third person but 'that depends who's free.' Hours: kitchen prep starts around 6am on event days; she generally doesn't take calls before 9am. Booking policy: wants a deposit 'sometime before the event, doesn't have to be right away' — technically she means 2 weeks out but rarely enforces it. Minimum guest count is supposed to be 15 but she's taken smaller jobs 'if it's a slow month.' Busy season is May-October; she sometimes overbooks weekends without realizing it until the week arrives. Genuinely unsure about: (1) whether she can legally serve alcohol-adjacent items (a rum cake she's been asked about) without a special permit — she's 'been meaning to call the county about that'; (2) how many actual events she can handle in one weekend before quality drops — she's said both 'we can do two no problem' and 'honestly one is plenty' in the same week. Her real pain point is she under-quotes on quantity constantly and ends up running out of food, so she's started 'padding' estimates but doesn't do it consistently.
